notes: Backwards compatible with schema 1.0 — every rule still carries `fail_if_found` and `weight`, so existing parsing continues to work. New fields (`action`, `protocol_section`, `match`, `scope`, `prescriber_note`, `patient_message`) are additive and can be ignored until the UI supports them.

match_defaults.comment: whole_word is the default and MUST NOT be relaxed for short acronyms. Substring matching on 'TIA' alone hits inertia, initiate, tibial, essential, differentiation. Substring on 'ACS' hits acetaminophen product names. Substring on 'MUSE' hits amuse/museum. Rules that genuinely need stem matching declare match:'stem' explicitly.

negation_guards.comment: Applied to every rule unless overridden. If a keyword hit falls within the guard window of one of these phrases, downgrade the hit from its declared action to 'review' and label it 'possible negation / family history — verify'. Never auto-clear; a prescriber confirms.

medication_status_guards.comment: Applied to rules with category 'medication'. SCR repeat/acute lists carry status. A discontinued nitrate is still a review, not a clear — patients restart. Everything else downgrades.

actions.reject: Hard stop. Consultation cannot be approved. Maps to a Section 5 rejection row.
actions.review: Prescriber must open and resolve before approval. Not an automatic decline.
actions.counsel: No barrier to supply. Surface to the prescriber so the counselling point is covered.

rules.name: PDE5 inhibitor allergy or previous serious adverse reaction
rules.prescriber_note: Absolute. Identical exclusion in all four SmPCs. Check the allergy free-text for excipients too — lactose appears in the sildenafil and tadalafil film coatings.
rules.patient_message: Our records suggest you may have had a reaction to a medicine of this type. We can't supply it safely without your GP reviewing this first.

rules.name: Ischaemic heart disease, angina, MI, revascularisation
rules.prescriber_note: The SmPCs bar only recent events — tadalafil MI within 90 days, avanafil MI/stroke/life-threatening arrhythmia within 6 months, plus unstable angina and angina during intercourse across the class. This protocol excludes any history at any distance as a SERVICE-LEVEL decision, and NICE would positively recommend offering a PDE5 inhibitor to an asymptomatic man more than 6 months post-MI. Record the date of the event in the decline note — you will want it if this exclusion is ever narrowed.
rules.patient_message: Because of a heart condition in your records, this treatment needs to be assessed in person. Please speak to your GP.

rules.name: Heart failure, cardiomyopathy, valve and outflow-tract disease
rules.prescriber_note: Left ventricular outflow obstruction (aortic stenosis, HOCM) and multiple system atrophy are named in the sildenafil and avanafil SmPCs as groups with increased susceptibility to vasodilators — these are the structural hits that matter most, not the historic valve murmur.

rules.name: Stroke and transient ischaemic attack
rules.prescriber_note: TIA and CVA MUST be whole-word matched. Substring matching on TIA produces hits on initiate, tibial, inertia, essential and differentiation, and will bury real hits in noise.

rules.name: Arrhythmia, congenital long QT, hypokalaemia
rules.prescriber_note: This rule is the SCR-side cover for the gap in Step 6, which asks about arrhythmia but not about congenital long QT or hypokalaemia. Vardenafil's SmPC documents dose-dependent QTc prolongation, so a man with congenital LQTS and no antiarrhythmic passes the whole online consultation. Until Step 6 is fixed, this rule is the only thing catching him. 'AF' whole-word only.

rules.name: Hypertension and hypotension
rules.prescriber_note: Where the SCR carries an actual BP reading, use the numbers, not the label: reject at 160/90 or higher, or below 90/50, and record which. Note that 160/90 is a SERVICE-LEVEL threshold — the only numerically defined SmPC figure in the class is avanafil's contraindication above 170/100. A coded diagnosis of hypertension without a recent reading is a review, not an automatic reject, unless an antihypertensive also appears (ED-MED-BP).

rules.name: Pulmonary arterial hypertension
rules.prescriber_note: Not in the current protocol and it should be. A man on Revatio or Adcirca is already taking a PDE5 inhibitor at a different licensed dose for a different indication — supplying a second is a duplicate, and riociguat is an absolute contraindication in all four SmPCs. Flag this to the Clinical Lead as a Section 5 addition.

rules.name: Non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy
keywords: non arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy
rules.prescriber_note: Contraindicated in all four SmPCs. The current tadalafil label goes further and notes that observational data suggest an increased risk of acute NAION in men with ED after PDE5 inhibitor exposure generally — relevant when counselling anyone with vascular risk factors, not only prior cases.

rules.name: Hereditary retinal degeneration
rules.prescriber_note: The SmPC contraindication for sildenafil, vardenafil and avanafil covers hereditary degenerative retinal disorders as a class, not retinitis pigmentosa specifically — the mechanism is retinal PDE6 abnormality, which several of these share. Tadalafil does not list it. Your Step 6 question was widened to match this in v2; this rule mirrors it.

rules.name: Hepatic impairment (any severity)
rules.prescriber_note: Correct SmPC position, which the protocol's rationale cell currently misstates: severe (Child-Pugh C) is contraindicated for sildenafil and avanafil; vardenafil has not been studied and is not recommended; tadalafil permits it after an individual benefit/risk evaluation. Mild-to-moderate is a dose reduction across all four. The service excludes every degree because severity can't be graded remotely and the correct cap differs by product.

rules.name: Renal impairment (any severity)
rules.prescriber_note: Correct SmPC position, which the protocol's rationale cell currently overstates: severe renal impairment (CrCl under 30) is contraindicated for avanafil ONLY. Sildenafil suggests 25 mg, tadalafil caps at 10 mg on demand with the daily regimen not recommended, vardenafil suggests a 5 mg start. Vardenafil is separately not recommended in dialysis. Where the SCR carries an eGFR, use the number.

rules.name: Priapism and predisposing haematological conditions
rules.protocol_section: 5 — Priapism history and blood conditions; Step 6
keywords: erection lasting longer than four hours
rules.prescriber_note: Prior priapism is an absolute exclusion on recurrence risk. The haematological conditions are SmPC cautions rather than contraindications and are excluded here as service policy — note that in the decline reason, because a man with sickle cell trait (as opposed to disease) is a materially different risk and may reasonably challenge it.

rules.name: Bleeding and clotting disorders
rules.protocol_section: 5 — Priapism history and blood conditions; Step 6
rules.prescriber_note: SmPC position across the class is that PDE5 inhibitors should be given to these patients only after a careful benefit-risk assessment — a caution, not a contraindication. Excluded here as service policy.

rules.name: Peptic, gastric or duodenal ulcer
rules.prescriber_note: REVIEW, not auto-reject — this is the one condition rule where the date matters and a keyword can't read it. Step 6 was corrected in v2 to a 12-month window ('active now, or active or treated in the last 12 months'). An eradication episode from 2004 is not an exclusion. Check the date on the SCR entry, then reject or proceed accordingly. Update Section 5's own wording to the same 12-month window — it still reads 'current or recent active', which is undefined.

rules.name: Penile deformity
rules.prescriber_note: SmPC caution, service-level exclusion. Refer to urology.

rules.name: Galactose intolerance and lactose excipient conditions
rules.prescriber_note: Excipient-specific. Sildenafil and tadalafil film coatings contain lactose; check the exact product being supplied, as not every brand or strength does. Ordinary lactose intolerance is NOT this — these are rare hereditary conditions.

rules.name: Diabetes mellitus
rules.changed_from_v1: Was fail_if_found: true. Changed because the Diabetes rejection box was removed from Section 5 in protocol v2.
rules.prescriber_note: Do NOT decline. NICE recommends offering a PDE5 inhibitor to men with ED and type 1 or type 2 diabetes, and no product in this protocol requires a dose adjustment — the tadalafil and avanafil SmPCs say so explicitly, and avanafil carries dedicated diabetic efficacy data (34–40% successful attempts against 21% placebo). Surface it so the counselling point is covered: response is less complete than in men without diabetes, and ED in diabetes is a marker of wider vascular risk warranting a GP review of glycaemic control, BP and lipids within six months.

rules.name: Mental health — unstable or unassessed
rules.protocol_section: 5 — Mental health (unstable or unassessed only); Step 5
rules.changed_from_v1: Was fail_if_found: true. Changed because protocol v2 narrowed Section 5 to unstable or unassessed conditions only — stable, assessed or treated conditions no longer exclude.
rules.prescriber_note: REVIEW, never auto-reject. A stable, GP-assessed, treated condition does not exclude. What you are looking for is instability or absence of assessment: a recent crisis contact, a psychiatric admission, a very recent diagnosis with no follow-up, or a new antidepressant start. Roughly one man in six has a history of depression and depression is itself one of the commonest causes of the ED being presented — declining on the diagnosis alone would exclude a large share of the population you exist to treat. Handle any self-harm or suicidality hit with care and route it to the prescriber directly rather than into an automated decline message.

rules.name: Recreational drug use
rules.protocol_section: 5 — Recreational drug or heavy alcohol use
rules.prescriber_note: Nitrites (poppers) are the only SmPC-level item here and they are absolute — additive vasodilation with a real risk of life-threatening hypotension. Everything else is service policy. Note that 'ketamine' and 'methadone' also appear as prescribed medicines; scope this rule to diagnosis and encounter text, not the repeat list, or you will decline a patient on prescribed methadone under a recreational-drug heading.

rules.name: Heavy or dependent alcohol use
rules.protocol_section: 5 — Recreational drug or heavy alcohol use
rules.prescriber_note: This rule is currently the ONLY working screen for heavy alcohol use. Section 5 and Section 7 both list it as a rejection, but the online consultation asks only the compound question 'Do you smoke or drink alcohol?' with both answers eligible — so a man drinking 60 units a week and a man having an occasional pint return the same answer and both proceed. Until Step 3 is split and quantified, every heavy-drinking decline depends on this SCR rule firing. Where the SCR carries an AUDIT-C or a units-per-week figure, use it: 35+ units a week rejects, 15–35 counsels.

rules.name: Nitrates, nitric oxide donors and guanylate cyclase stimulators
rules.prescriber_note: Corlanor was removed — it is a brand of ivabradine, a funny-current inhibitor, not a nitrate or NO donor, and it carries no PDE5 contraindication. Leaving it in generates a false decline on a rationale that cannot be defended. This is the one rule where a 'discontinued' status must NOT downgrade the action: patients restart GTN, and a spray sitting in a drawer is the classic fatal combination.

rules.name: Other PDE5 inhibitors and ED treatments
rules.prescriber_note: MUSE must be whole-word and case-sensitive — substring matching hits amuse, museum and amused. A live PDE5 inhibitor on the SCR is a duplicate-supply risk, not just an interaction: check whether it is a Revatio/Adcirca PAH prescription (see ED-CV-PAH) or an existing ED supply from another provider.

rules.name: Dapoxetine (premature ejaculation)
rules.protocol_section: 7 — Dapoxetine row (NOT yet in Section 5 or Step 7)
rules.prescriber_note: NEW RULE and the most important addition in this file. Dapoxetine was added to the protocol's Section 7 interaction table in v2 but was NOT added to Section 5's medicine list or to the Step 7 question — so nothing in the online consultation asks about it, and a patient will answer 'no' to 'any other treatment for erectile dysfunction' entirely honestly, because dapoxetine isn't one. EveryDayMeds supplies dapoxetine through EDM-PE-01, so the same patient can hold both accounts. Both classes lower blood pressure, dapoxetine carries a recognised risk of orthostatic hypotension and syncope, and its SmPC advises against concomitant PDE5 inhibitor use. Until Step 7 is fixed, this SCR rule is the only block in the dangerous direction — and it will only fire if the dapoxetine was prescribed somewhere that reaches the SCR.

rules.name: Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors
rules.prescriber_note: Clarithromycin belongs HERE, not in the moderate group — the avanafil SmPC names it among the potent inhibitors whose co-administration is contraindicated. Your Section 7 table currently lists clarithromycin in both rows; the SmPC settles it as potent. Magnitude: ketoconazole raises avanafil AUC 14-fold and ritonavir 13-fold, and both extend its half-life to around 9 hours. Contraindicated outright for avanafil and vardenafil; sildenafil and tadalafil call for a dose cap, and this protocol rejects across the class.

rules.name: Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors
rules.prescriber_note: Diltiazem and verapamil were missing from your v1 file entirely — they appear in neither the moderate CYP3A4 list nor the blood pressure list, so a man on diltiazem was passing the SCR scan completely. They are named in the avanafil SmPC as moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors capping avanafil at 100 mg with a minimum 48-hour interval, so this is a pharmacokinetic interaction, not merely the additive hypotensive effect the protocol's rationale describes for calcium-channel blockers generally. If the general antihypertensive exclusion is ever relaxed, these two must be carved out and kept.

rules.name: Doxazosin
rules.prescriber_note: Split out from the general alpha-blocker rule because it is genuinely different. The tadalafil SmPC states the combination with doxazosin is not recommended — the blood-pressure-lowering effect is significantly increased, lasts at least twelve hours and may be symptomatic including syncope. With sildenafil, additional standing BP falls of up to 11/4 mmHg and symptomatic postural hypotension have been reported. This is a labelled interaction, not a service-level simplification, and must stay a reject even if the rest of the class is relaxed.

rules.name: Alpha-blockers other than doxazosin
rules.prescriber_note: Manageable under the SmPCs: stabilise on the alpha-blocker first, then start low — sildenafil 25 mg, vardenafil 5 mg, avanafil 50 mg. Vardenafil's label in fact permits concurrent dosing with tamsulosin or alfuzosin at any time, and tadalafil's doxazosin effect was not reproduced with either. Rejected here as service policy. Tamsulosin is by a wide margin the commonest alpha-blocker in the 50–75 age band, so if a decline-rate exercise is ever run this is the highest-volume, lowest-risk carve-out available anywhere in the protocol. Note Combodart and Vesomni are combination products containing tamsulosin.

rules.name: Antihypertensives other than alpha-blockers
rules.prescriber_note: Be honest in the decline note that this is a commercial-simplicity decision, not an evidential one. Pooled sildenafil data showed no difference in side-effect profile against placebo across diuretics, beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors, ARBs and calcium-channel blockers; tadalafil phase 3 data showed no difference in adverse events with or without antihypertensives; avanafil with enalapril or amlodipine produced mean maximum supine falls of 2/3 and 1/-1 mmHg. Diltiazem and verapamil are handled separately under ED-MED-CYP3A4-MOD because they are a different kind of interaction.

rules.name: Sacubitril/valsartan
rules.protocol_section: Not yet in Section 5 — flag for addition
rules.prescriber_note: Not in the protocol and it should be named. Adding a single sildenafil dose to steady-state sacubitril/valsartan produced a significantly greater blood-pressure fall than sacubitril/valsartan alone, and the sildenafil SmPC now advises caution on initiation. It is not caught by 'medicines used to treat high blood pressure' in Step 7 because patients describe it as a heart failure medicine. These patients are excluded anyway by the heart failure row, so this is belt-and-braces — but it belongs in Section 5 by name.

rules.name: Enzyme-inducing medicines
rules.prescriber_note: For sildenafil and tadalafil this is loss of efficacy rather than a safety concern — rifampicin cuts tadalafil exposure by 88%, bosentan cuts sildenafil exposure by around 63%. For avanafil the position is stronger: the effect has not been evaluated and the SmPC states concomitant use is not recommended. Bosentan is bidirectional — sildenafil raises bosentan exposure by around 50%. Note that etravirine and efavirenz are inducers, not inhibitors; your Step 7 question currently lists etravirine alongside the protease inhibitors, which is the wrong pharmacological group.

rules.name: Anticoagulants and antiplatelets
rules.prescriber_note: Flagged as under review. There is no pharmacological basis for this exclusion in any of the four labels: sildenafil and tadalafil showed no significant interaction with warfarin and no effect on warfarin-induced prothrombin time; neither potentiated aspirin's effect on bleeding time; avanafil's label states PDE5 inhibitors do not appear to affect bleeding time alone or with aspirin, and that no interaction is expected with rivaroxaban or apixaban. Low-dose aspirin and clopidogrel are extremely common in men over 50. If this moves to COUNSEL, change action here to 'counsel' and set fail_if_found false — the counselling point is that epistaxis, haematuria and haematospermia are recognised uncommon effects and more noticeable on an anticoagulant. The bleeding-disorder and peptic-ulcer rules stay as they are; those ARE SmPC-sourced.

rules.name: Antiarrhythmics and QT-prolonging medicines
rules.prescriber_note: Vardenafil's SmPC documents dose-dependent QTc prolongation and contraindicates concomitant class Ia and class III antiarrhythmics; this protocol rejects across the class rather than substituting an alternative product. Digoxin and ivabradine are included as markers of underlying cardiac disease rather than as QT interactions — they will be caught by ED-CV-ARRHYTHMIA-QT anyway, but a man's SCR sometimes carries the drug without the coded diagnosis. Dronedarone additionally appears under ED-MED-CYP3A4-MOD.

rules.name: Theophylline and aminophylline
rules.prescriber_note: The weakest-supported exclusion in the medicines list. Tadalafil's SmPC documents no pharmacokinetic interaction and only a 3.5 bpm heart-rate increase judged of no clinical significance; sildenafil's says there are simply no data on the interaction with non-specific phosphodiesterase inhibitors. Rejected as service policy. Worth reviewing alongside the anticoagulant row.

rules.name: Diabetes medicines (context only)
rules.prescriber_note: Detection only, never a decline. Diabetes is frequently visible in the repeat list when the diagnosis code is absent or historic. Use it to trigger the diabetes counselling point in Section 6 and to prompt the GP-review recommendation. Note also that semaglutide, liraglutide and dulaglutide may indicate weight management rather than diabetes — check against the EveryDayMeds weight management record before assuming.

rules.name: Antidepressants and SSRIs (context only)
rules.prescriber_note: Not an exclusion — surface it for two reasons. First, an antidepressant with no recent review, or one started in the last three months, is the practical marker of the 'unstable or unassessed' mental health condition Section 5 now excludes; a long-standing stable repeat is not. Second, SSRIs and SNRIs are themselves a common cause of ED, so the presenting complaint may be drug-induced and worth raising with the GP rather than treated around. Antipsychotics and lithium raise the same question more strongly.

rules.name: Prostate disease and pelvic surgery (context)
rules.prescriber_note: Review, not decline. This is one of the largest genuine ED populations and NICE NG131 — already cited in your References — specifically addresses PDE5 inhibitors after prostate cancer treatment. Two things to flag: response rates are markedly lower after non-nerve-sparing radical prostatectomy (avanafil trials showed 23–26% successful attempts against 9% placebo), so expectations need managing; and androgen deprivation therapy causes loss of libido that a PDE5 inhibitor will not treat, which is exactly the misunderstanding declaration item 3 now exists to address. Tadalafil's own label notes it is not known whether it is effective after pelvic surgery or radical non-nerve-sparing prostatectomy.

rules.name: Neurological and endocrine causes (context)
rules.prescriber_note: Review, not decline. NICE recommends offering a PDE5 inhibitor to men with ED and multiple sclerosis, and tadalafil carries spinal cord injury efficacy data (48% successful attempts against 17% placebo), so neither is a reason to withhold. Testosterone and hypogonadism sit outside this protocol's scope — the man is not excluded, but if he is on TRT the prescriber should note it, and an untreated low testosterone presenting as loss of desire rather than loss of erection needs the GP, not a PDE5 inhibitor. Your v1 file had testosterone products under the PDE5 rule with fail_if_found true, which would have wrongly declined every man on TRT.
